
Many expensive steps produce files rather than R values: alignments, index
files, model checkpoints, rendered reports. This vignette shows how a shared
computation writes files, how they come back on a hit, and how to identify
input files by their contents.

```{r}
library(targets)
library(tarshare)

root <- tempfile("tarshare-files-")
dir.create(root)
cache_path <- file.path(root, "cache")
cache <- shared_cache(cache_path)
```

## Writing files

Use `format = "file"` and write every output below `shared_path()`. Inside a
file computation, `shared_path("name")` returns a path in a private staging
directory and creates any parent directories. Return the paths you want back,
or `shared_path()` for the whole directory:

```{r}
values <- c(3, 5, 8, 13)
paths <- shared_run({
  cat("computing\n")
  summary <- c(n = length(values), mean = mean(values))
  saveRDS(summary, shared_path("summary.rds"))
  writeLines(format(summary), shared_path("summary.txt"))
  writeLines("summary.rds summary.txt", shared_path("MANIFEST"))
  c(rds = shared_path("summary.rds"), text = shared_path("summary.txt"))
}, cache, format = "file")
basename(paths)
readRDS(paths[["rds"]])
```

The returned paths point into the cache, not into staging. The whole staging
directory was stored, so the manifest travelled with the two files you asked
for even though it was not returned:

```{r}
list.files(dirname(paths[["rds"]]))
```

A hit returns the same paths without running the command:

```{r}
paths_again <- shared_run({
  cat("computing\n")
  summary <- c(n = length(values), mean = mean(values))
  saveRDS(summary, shared_path("summary.rds"))
  writeLines(format(summary), shared_path("summary.txt"))
  writeLines("summary.rds summary.txt", shared_path("MANIFEST"))
  c(rds = shared_path("summary.rds"), text = shared_path("summary.txt"))
}, cache, format = "file")
identical(paths, paths_again)
```

## The files belong to the cache

Cached files are immutable by contract: downstream steps read them and write
their own outputs elsewhere. The cache does not change file permissions to
enforce this, but with the default `verify = TRUE` every lookup re-hashes the
bundle. A bundle that no longer matches its record is treated as missing, the
command runs again, and the damaged entry is replaced:

```{r}
writeLines("edited in place", paths[["text"]])
paths <- shared_run({
  cat("computing\n")
  summary <- c(n = length(values), mean = mean(values))
  saveRDS(summary, shared_path("summary.rds"))
  writeLines(format(summary), shared_path("summary.txt"))
  writeLines("summary.rds summary.txt", shared_path("MANIFEST"))
  c(rds = shared_path("summary.rds"), text = shared_path("summary.txt"))
}, cache, format = "file")
readLines(paths[["text"]])
```

Turn verification off only when something else guarantees immutability, such
as a read-only export of the cache. Record integrity and bundle completeness
are checked either way.

Outputs must be created inside staging. A path from anywhere else is
rejected before anything is published:

```{r}
tryCatch(
  shared_run({
    elsewhere <- tempfile()
    writeLines("x", elsewhere)
    elsewhere
  }, cache, format = "file"),
  error = conditionMessage
)
```

Symbolic links inside the bundle are rejected too, and the cache never
rewrites file contents, so avoid writing the staging path into a file.

## Values that are not self-contained

The default `format = "rds"` is for values that can be serialised and read
back on their own. Live resources are refused:

```{r}
tryCatch(shared_run(new.env(), cache), error = conditionMessage)
```

An R object that merely contains a path does not preserve the file behind the
path. Write such files through `format = "file"` instead.

## File targets in a pipeline

In a pipeline, a `format = "file"` shared target behaves like a targets file
target: its value is the vector of cache paths, and downstream targets use
them like any other file. The pipeline below writes a table and counts its
rows:

```{r}
script <- file.path(root, "_targets.R")
tar_helper(script, {
  library(targets)
  library(tarshare)
  cache <- shared_cache(!!cache_path)
  list(
    tar_target(values, c(3, 5, 8, 13)),
    tar_shared(values_table, {
      path <- shared_path("values.csv")
      utils::write.csv(data.frame(value = values), path, row.names = FALSE)
      path
    }, cache, format = "file"),
    tar_target(n_rows, nrow(utils::read.csv(values_table)))
  )
})
store_1 <- file.path(root, "store-1")
tar_make(script = script, store = store_1)
tar_read(n_rows, store = store_1)
```

A second store gets the table from the cache. The cheap downstream target
still runs, because it is an ordinary target in a fresh store:

```{r}
store_2 <- file.path(root, "store-2")
tar_make(script = script, store = store_2)
identical(tar_read(values_table, store = store_1), tar_read(values_table, store = store_2))
```

Because the shared target has `format = "file"`, targets also watches the
cache files, and the usual skipping applies while they are unchanged.

## Identifying input files

A plain character path is an ordinary value: the key records the string, not
the file. `shared_file()` replaces it with a descriptor that carries a content
hash per path and still works as a path. See `vignette("identity")` for why
this matters.

```{r}
sample_a <- file.path(root, "sample-a.txt")
sample_b <- file.path(root, "sample-b.txt")
writeLines(c("3", "5"), sample_a)
writeLines(c("8", "13"), sample_b)
inputs <- shared_file(c(a = sample_a, b = sample_b))
inputs
```

Descriptors keep names, order and ids together under subsetting and
concatenation, so a pipeline can pass them around as it would any paths:

```{r}
inputs["b"]
c(inputs["b"], inputs["a"])
```

Replacement is refused: rebuild the descriptor with `shared_file()` when a path
changes. `as.character()` drops the ids and gives back ordinary paths.

Hashing a large file on every graph construction is wasteful when an
immutable identity already exists, such as a hash from a sample sheet or an
object version. Pass it as `id` and the file is not read:

```{r}
registered <- shared_file(sample_a, id = "sha256:established-upstream")
attr(registered, "tarshare_id")
```

Supplying an id is an assertion that the id describes the bytes used. The
cache does not check it. Directories cannot be hashed automatically and always
need an explicit id.

Use content identity only when the result does not depend on the file's name
or location. If a name carries meaning, such as a sample label, declare it in
`context` as well.

```{r, include = FALSE}
unlink(root, recursive = TRUE)
```
